steps.message: You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

Please solve this issue: Whenever a book's cover changes, `Book::CoverProcessingJob` (in `app/jobs`)
is kicked off from the `Book` model and stamps the cover's SHA-256
fingerprint into the blob's metadata. In production it fails intermittently:
the worker picks it up before the database transaction that attached the
cover has committed, finds no file, and raises
`ActiveStorage::FileNotFoundError`. Worse, when a save inside a larger
transaction is rolled back, the work for the never-committed cover is still
handed off — and errors on every retry. The search entry a book edit
refreshes goes the same way, off the same handover.

Fix when that background work is handed off. It should not be handed off
until the edit that kicked it off has committed, never while that edit is
still open — and if the edit is abandoned, it must never be handed off at
all.

The nightly importer runs the same edit over a whole batch, and applies the
batch all or nothing, so this has to hold there too. One thing must survive an
abandoned batch, though: the operator still hears that their import did not go
through. Losing that is how a failed import goes unnoticed until somebody asks.

On a successful edit the outcome is unchanged: the work still runs, the same
fingerprint is stamped and the search entry is refreshed. No new tables or
columns, and `bin/rails test` stays green; don't edit it.

## Testing Conventions

### Use Existing Fixtures
Prefer using existing fixtures over creating new records in tests. For example, use `leaves(:welcome_page)` instead of `books(:handbook).press Page.new(body: "..."), title: "..."`.

### URL Helpers in Tests
Use `_path` helpers instead of `_url` helpers in controller/integration tests unless you need to test across different hosts or explicitly need the full URL.

**Preferred:**
```ruby
get book_slug_path(books(:handbook))
```

**Avoid:**
```ruby
get book_slug_url(books(:handbook))
```

### Response Body Assertions
Use `assert_in_body` and `assert_not_in_body` to check if text is present or absent in the response body without DOM manipulation.

**Preferred:**
```ruby
assert_in_body "Expected content"
assert_not_in_body "Unexpected content"
```

**Avoid:**
```ruby
assert_includes response.body, "Expected content"
assert_not_includes response.body, "Unexpected content"
```

## Controller Conventions

### Simplified respond_to Blocks
When using `respond_to` with default rendering, omit the `{ render }` block as it's implied.

**Preferred:**
```ruby
def show
  respond_to do |format|
    format.html
    format.md
  end
end
```

**Avoid:**
```ruby
def show
  respond_to do |format|
    format.html { render }
    format.md { render }
  end
end
```

class Book < ApplicationRecord
  include Accessable, Editing, Sluggable

  has_many :leaves, dependent: :destroy
  has_one_attached :cover, dependent: :purge_later

  scope :ordered, -> { order(:title) }
  scope :published, -> { where(published: true) }

  enum :theme, %w[ black blue green magenta orange violet white ].index_by(&:itself), suffix: true, default: :blue

  def press(leafable, leaf_params)

  def markable

  end

module Book::Editing
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  def apply_edit(attributes)
    transaction do
      update!(attributes)
      Book::SearchIndexJob.perform_later(self)
      Book::CoverProcessingJob.set(wait: 5.seconds).perform_later(self) if attributes[:cover].present?
    end
  end
end

module Book::Accessable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    has_many :accesses, dependent: :destroy
    scope :with_everyone_access, -> { where(everyone_access: true) }
  end

  class_methods do
    def accessable_or_published(user: Current.user)
      if user.present?
        accessable_or_published_books
      else
        published
      end
    end

    def accessable_or_published_books(user: Current.user)
      user.books.or(published).distinct
    end
  end

  def accessable?(user: Current.user)
    accesses.exists?(user: user)
  end

  def editable?(user: Current.user)
    access_for(user: user)&.editor? || user&.administrator?
  end

  def access_for(user: Current.user)
    accesses.find_by(user: user)
  end

  def update_access(editors:, readers:)
    editors = Set.new(editors)
    readers = Set.new(everyone_access? ? User.active.ids : readers)

    all = editors + readers
    all_accesses = all.collect { |user_id|
      { user_id: user_id, level: editors.include?(user_id) ? :editor : :reader }
    }

    accesses.upsert_all(all_accesses, unique_by: [ :book_id, :user_id ])
    accesses.where.not(user_id: all).delete_all
  end
end

class BooksController < ApplicationController
  allow_unauthenticated_access only: %i[ index show ]

  before_action :ensure_index_is_not_empty, only: :index
  before_action :set_book, only: %i[ show edit update destroy ]
  before_action :set_users, only: %i[ new edit ]
  before_action :ensure_editable, only: %i[ edit update destroy ]

  def index
    @books = Book.accessable_or_published.ordered
  end

  def new
    @book = Book.new
  end

  def create
    book = Book.create! book_params
    update_accesses(book)

    redirect_to book_slug_url(book)
  end

  def show
    @leaves = @book.leaves.active.with_leafables.positioned

    respond_to do |format|
      format.html
      format.md
    end
  end

  def edit
  end

  def update
    @book.apply_edit(book_params)
    update_accesses(@book)
    remove_cover if params[:remove_cover] == "true"

    redirect_to book_slug_url(@book)
  end

  def destroy
    @book.destroy

    redirect_to root_url
  end

  private
    def set_book
      @book = Book.accessable_or_published.find params[:id]
    end

    def set_users
      @users = User.active.ordered
    end

    def ensure_editable
      head :forbidden unless @book.editable?
    end

    def ensure_index_is_not_empty
      if !signed_in? && Book.published.none?
        require_authentication
      end
    end

    def book_params
      params.require(:book).permit(:title, :subtitle, :author, :cover, :remove_cover, :everyone_access, :theme)
    end

    def update_accesses(book)
      editors = [ Current.user.id, *params[:editor_ids]&.map(&:to_i) ]
      readers = [ Current.user.id, *params[:reader_ids]&.map(&:to_i) ]

      book.update_access(editors: editors, readers: readers)
    end

    def remove_cover
      @book.cover.purge
    end
end

class Books::ImportsController < ApplicationController
  def create
    Book.transaction do
      book_batch.each do |id, attributes|
        Book.accessable_or_published.find(id).apply_edit(attributes)
      end
    rescue StandardError => error
      Books::ImportFailureJob.perform_later(Current.user.id, error.message)
      raise
    end

    redirect_to root_url
  end

  private
    def book_batch
      params.require(:books).each_pair.map do |id, attributes|
        [ id, attributes.permit(:title, :subtitle, :author, :cover) ]
      end
    end
end

      # automatically defers the enqueue to after the transaction commits.

      #  - false forces the job to be queued immediately.

    end

    # Includes the +perform_later+ method for job initialization.
    module ClassMethods

      # Integer, Float, NilClass, TrueClass, FalseClass, BigDecimal, Symbol, Date,

      # Hash, ActiveSupport::HashWithIndifferentAccess, Array, Range, or
      # GlobalID::Identification instances, although this can be extended by adding
      # custom serializers.

      # Job#arguments or +false+ if the enqueue did not succeed.
      #
      # After the attempted enqueue, the job will be yielded to an optional block.
      #

      def perform_later(...)

  # Registers a block to be called after all the current transactions have been
  # committed.
  #
  # If there is no currently open transaction, the block is called immediately.
  #
  # If there are multiple nested transactions, the block is called after the outermost one
  # has been committed,
  #
  # If any of the currently open transactions is rolled back, the block is never called.
  #
  # If multiple transactions are open across multiple databases, the block will be invoked
  # if and once all of them have been committed. But note that nesting transactions across
  # two distinct databases is a sharding anti-pattern that comes with a world of hurts.
  def self.after_all_transactions_commit(&block)
    open_transactions = all_open_transactions

    if open_transactions.empty?
      yield
    elsif open_transactions.size == 1
      open_transactions.first.after_commit(&block)
    else
      count = open_transactions.size
      callback = -> do
        count -= 1
        block.call if count.zero?
      end
      open_transactions.each do |t|
        t.after_commit(&callback)
      end
      open_transactions = nil # rubocop:disable Lint/UselessAssignment avoid holding it in the closure
    end
  end

  def self.all_open_transactions # :nodoc:
    open_transactions = []
    Base.connection_handler.each_connection_pool do |pool|
      if active_connection = pool.active_connection
        current_transaction = active_connection.current_transaction

        if current_transaction.open? && current_transaction.joinable?
          open_transactions << current_transaction
        end
      end
    end
    open_transactions
  end

class QueueAdapterHandoverTimingTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  include ActionDispatch::TestProcess::FixtureFile

  class InspectingAdapter < ActiveJob::QueueAdapters::AbstractAdapter
    attr_reader :observations

    def initialize
      @observations = []
    end

    def enqueue(job)
      record_observation(job)
    end

    def enqueue_at(job, _timestamp)
      record_observation(job)
    end

    private
      def record_observation(job)
        book_arg = job.arguments.first
        open_tx_count = ActiveRecord.all_open_transactions.size
        blob_exists_in_service = if book_arg.is_a?(Book) && book_arg.cover.attached?
          book_arg.cover.blob.service.exist?(book_arg.cover.blob.key)
        end
        @observations << {
          job_class: job.class,
          open_transactions: open_tx_count,
          blob_exists_in_service: blob_exists_in_service
        }
      end
  end

    end
  end
end

class RealTransactionCrossConnectionTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  self.use_transactional_tests = false
  include ActionDispatch::TestProcess::FixtureFile

  class WorkerThreadAdapter < ActiveJob::QueueAdapters::AbstractAdapter
    attr_reader :errors, :completed

    def initialize
      @errors = []
      @completed = []
    end

    def enqueue(job)
      run_in_separate_thread(job)
    end

    def enqueue_at(job, _timestamp)
      run_in_separate_thread(job)
    end

    private
      def run_in_separate_thread(job)
        serialized = job.serialize
        Thread.new do
          ActiveRecord::Base.connection_pool.with_connection do
            ActiveJob::Base.execute(serialized)
            @completed << serialized["job_class"]
          end
        rescue => e
          @errors << e
        end.join
      end
  end

  setup do
    @original_cache = Rails.cache
    Rails.cache = ActiveSupport::Cache::MemoryStore.new
  end

  teardown do
    Rails.cache = @original_cache
  end

  test "worker on separate DB connection sees committed book and cover immediately on handoff" do
    worker_adapter = WorkerThreadAdapter.new
    old_adapter = ActiveJob::Base.queue_adapter
    book = Book.create!(title: "Real Tx Book")
    begin
      ActiveJob::Base.disable_test_adapter
      ActiveJob::Base.queue_adapter = worker_adapter

      cover_path = Rails.root.join("test/fixtures/files/white-rabbit.webp")
      expected_sha = Digest::SHA256.file(cover_path).hexdigest
      cover = fixture_file_upload("white-rabbit.webp", "image/webp")

      book.apply_edit("title" => "Committed Real Tx", "cover" => cover)

      assert_empty worker_adapter.errors, "Worker thread encountered errors: #{worker_adapter.errors.inspect}"
      assert_equal [ "Book::SearchIndexJob", "Book::CoverProcessingJob" ], worker_adapter.completed
      assert_equal expected_sha, book.reload.cover.blob.metadata["sha256"]
      assert_equal "Committed Real Tx", Rails.cache.read("search_index/book/#{book.id}")
    ensure
      ActiveJob::Base.queue_adapter = old_adapter
      book&.destroy
    end
  end

  test "replacing an existing cover and rolling back keeps original cover and hands off nothing" do
    worker_adapter = WorkerThreadAdapter.new
    old_adapter = ActiveJob::Base.queue_adapter
    book = Book.create!(title: "Existing Cover Book")
    begin
      ActiveJob::Base.disable_test_adapter
      ActiveJob::Base.queue_adapter = worker_adapter

      cover1_path = Rails.root.join("test/fixtures/files/reading.webp")
      sha1 = Digest::SHA256.file(cover1_path).hexdigest
      book.apply_edit(title: "V1", cover: fixture_file_upload("reading.webp", "image/webp"))

        raise ActiveRecord::Rollback

      assert_equal "V1", book.reload.title
      assert_equal sha1, book.cover.blob.metadata["sha256"]
    ensure
      ActiveJob::Base.queue_adapter = old_adapter
      book&.destroy
    end
  end
end

I have resolved the issue so that background work from book edits is only handed off after the enclosing database transaction commits, and never when an edit or batch import is rolled back, while ensuring import failure notifications still go through:

1. **Defer job handoff until transaction commit (`config/application.rb`)**: Enabled `config.active_job.enqueue_after_transaction_commit = true` so jobs enqueued inside transactions (including `Book::CoverProcessingJob` and `Book::SearchIndexJob` in `Book::Editing#apply_edit`, whether standalone or nested inside a larger batch transaction) are not handed off until all open transactions commit—after ActiveStorage has uploaded the attached cover blob—and are dropped if the transaction rolls back.

3. **Preserve import failure reporting on abandoned batches (`app/jobs/books/import_failure_job.rb`, `app/controllers/books/imports_controller.rb`)**: Configured `self.enqueue_after_transaction_commit = false` on `Books::ImportFailureJob` and rescued outside `Book.transaction` in `Books::ImportsController#create` so failed batch imports always notify the operator while rolling back all book edits and discarding their queued jobs.
